citation: CDC, U.S. Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use, 2024, MMWR Recommendations and Reports Vol. 73, No. 4 (verify current edition at cdc.gov)

conditions.notes: Not applicable — none of these methods are initiated during a known pregnancy.

conditions.condition: Postpartum, <21 days, not breastfeeding, no other VTE risk factors
conditions.notes: VTE risk is highest in the first 3 weeks postpartum, which is why CHC is restricted here.

conditions.condition: Postpartum, 21-42 days, not breastfeeding, no other VTE risk factors
Postpartum, with additional VTE risk factors (e.g., prior VTE, transfusion at delivery, BMI ≥30, preeclampsia)
conditions.notes: CHC stays restricted through roughly 42 days when additional clot risk factors are present.

conditions.condition: IUD insertion, immediate postplacental (<10 minutes after delivery)
conditions.notes: Applies specifically to timing of IUD placement, not to the non-IUD methods.

conditions.condition: IUD insertion, 10 minutes to <4 weeks postpartum
conditions.notes: Higher expulsion risk in this window, not a safety contraindication.
Contraindicates IUD placement specifically; non-IUD methods are unaffected.
Progestin-only methods get a cautious category 2 in the earliest days due to theoretical neonatal exposure concerns.
CHC remains a 2 while breastfeeding due to a possible, likely small, effect on milk supply.
Caution reflects nulliparity/expulsion risk for IUDs and bone-density theoretical concern with DMPA, not a strict contraindication.
Reflects rising background cardiovascular risk with age rather than age itself.

conditions.condition: Multiple risk factors for arterial cardiovascular disease (e.g., older age, smoking, diabetes, hypertension combined)
conditions.notes: CHC category depends on the number and severity of risk factors present.

conditions.condition: Bariatric surgery, malabsorptive procedure (e.g., Roux-en-Y gastric bypass)
conditions.notes: Concern is reduced absorption of oral hormonal methods; non-oral methods are preferred.

conditions.condition: Bariatric surgery, restrictive procedure (e.g., sleeve gastrectomy, banding)
History of hypertensive disorder of pregnancy, now normotensive
VTE, history of, not on anticoagulation
Known thrombogenic mutation (e.g., factor V Leiden, prothrombin mutation, protein C/S or antithrombin deficiency)
conditions.notes: Routine thrombophilia screening is not recommended before starting CHC; this applies when a mutation is already known.

conditions.condition: Ischemic heart disease, current or history
conditions.notes: Category is higher (worse) for new initiation than for continuation in someone already stable on a method.

conditions.condition: Valvular heart disease, complicated (pulmonary hypertension, atrial fibrillation, history of endocarditis)
Peripartum cardiomyopathy, normal or mildly reduced function
conditions.notes: CHC category improves somewhat over time from diagnosis; use caution early on.

conditions.condition: Peripartum cardiomyopathy, moderately or severely reduced function

conditions.notes: Acceptable to start (2) but category worsens to 3 if migraines continue/worsen on CHC.
Aura is an independent marker of elevated stroke risk with estrogen-containing methods.
Category reflects the condition itself; enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants (phenytoin, carbamazepine, topiramate, barbiturates) separately reduce efficacy of CHC/POP/implant.
Hormonal methods are avoided with active hormone-sensitive disease; copper IUD is unaffected.

conditions.condition: Breast cancer, past, no evidence of disease ≥5 years

conditions.notes: Category improves once the mass has been evaluated.
IUD insertion is deferred with an active cervical lesion (4), but continuing a device already in place is generally fine (2).
Same insertion-vs-continuation logic as cervical cancer applies.
Distorted cavity precludes IUD placement.

conditions.condition: Anatomic abnormality distorting the uterine cavity (e.g., bicornuate uterus)

conditions.notes: New IUD insertion is deferred during active PID (4); a device already in place can usually stay (2) while treating.

conditions.condition: Pelvic inflammatory disease, past, no current risk factors
Current purulent cervicitis or chlamydial/gonococcal infection
High individual risk of STI exposure
conditions.notes: None of these methods protect against STIs; barrier method counseling should accompany any choice.

conditions.condition: HIV, high risk or infected, clinically well on antiretroviral therapy
conditions.notes: Certain antiretrovirals can lower hormonal method efficacy; check for drug interactions.

conditions.condition: AIDS, clinically unwell, not on antiretroviral therapy
conditions.notes: IUD insertion caution reflects infection risk/immune status; continuation is less restricted.

conditions.condition: Diabetes, history of gestational diabetes only
Diabetes, type 1 or 2, without vascular disease
Diabetes with nephropathy, retinopathy, neuropathy, other vascular disease, or duration >20 years
Gestational trophoblastic disease, decreasing or undetectable hCG
Gestational trophoblastic disease, persistently elevated hCG or malignant disease
conditions.notes: Avoid uterine instrumentation; non-IUD methods are not restricted.

conditions.condition: Viral hepatitis, chronic or carrier state
Liver tumor, benign focal nodular hyperplasia
History of cholestasis, related to prior combined hormonal contraceptive use

conditions.notes: Category can rise with malabsorption, strictures, or concurrent corticosteroid/other risk factors.
DMPA may have added benefit for pain crisis frequency in this population.
Reflects heavier menstrual bleeding typically seen with copper IUD.

conditions.condition: Systemic lupus erythematosus, positive or unknown antiphospholipid antibodies

conditions.notes: Copper IUD caution relates to bleeding risk with thrombocytopenia, not clotting.

conditions.condition: Systemic lupus erythematosus, no other complications

conditions.notes: IUD caution relates to theoretical infection risk on immunosuppression.

conditions.condition: Solid organ transplant, complicated (graft failure, rejection, cardiac allograft vasculopathy)

conditions.notes: LNG-IUD and continuous CHC are often chosen for symptom control, but all methods carry category 1 for safety.
New IUD insertion is deferred until the cause is evaluated; continuing an existing device is less restricted.
Hepatic enzyme induction lowers efficacy of oral/patch/ring and implant; DMPA and IUDs are not affected.

conditions.condition: Enzyme-inducing anticonvulsant therapy (e.g., phenytoin, carbamazepine, barbiturates, topiramate)

conditions.notes: Specific interactions vary by regimen; verify against current ART drug-interaction tables.
